_comment: SHAPE REFERENCE, NOT A RECORD. This is the template copy: it deliberately lists ZERO archives, because a scaffolded case that shipped a filled-in list would assert checksums for binaries it never built. Do not hand-author entries here or in the case copy -- the file is GENERATED by scanning the archive directory and the PROVENANCE.txt inside each one (tools/binary_archive_manifest.py --generate), and a hand-typed SHA256 is an assertion nobody can check, which is the exact problem this file exists to remove.
_why_this_file_exists: model-evolution step 3.5 requires a run to bind to an ARCHIVED, content-addressed executable rather than the live build path. EcoSIM (like PFLOTRAN and ATS) has ONE build output that every rebuild overwrites in place, and a queued scheduler job resolves its executable at RUN time -- so a rebuild between submit and start swaps the model under a running ensemble and nothing reports it. The archives are NOT regenerable: a recompile can perturb floating point, so a rebuilt binary is a DIFFERENT artifact, not the same one. They are also too large for git (~25 MB each) and would permanently bloat a fork of an upstream scientific code. So git tracks this MANIFEST instead -- a few KB giving, per archive, its label, source commit, size and SHA256. That buys the three things tracking was for: a permanent record that each binary existed, a checksum to detect alteration or swap, and enough provenance to say which build produced a result.
_the_manifest_is_PER_MODEL_not_per_case: Read this before expecting a scaffolded case to fill its own copy. One EcoSIM build archive is SHARED by every EcoSIM case, so the live manifest is keyed by MODEL, and its path is hardcoded in tools/binary_archive_manifest.py::ARCHIVES. Scaffolding a new case does NOT create or register a new manifest, and running --generate does NOT write into the new case's config/. Two consequences: (1) this copy stays empty and inert -- nothing reads it, since the tool only ever opens the path in ARCHIVES; (2) if a case ever needs its own manifest (a private archive root, a different machine), that is a code change to ARCHIVES, not a file you can drop in here.

_what_makes_verify_FAIL.M1: an archive in the manifest is MISSING from disk -> ERROR
_what_makes_verify_FAIL.M2: a binary's SHA256 differs from the manifest -> ERROR (altered or swapped)
_what_makes_verify_FAIL.M3: a binary's SHA256 differs from its own PROVENANCE.txt -> ERROR (internally inconsistent)
_what_makes_verify_FAIL.M4: an archive exists on disk but is ABSENT from the manifest -> WARN (re-generate)
_what_makes_verify_FAIL.M5: an archive directory has no binary, or no PROVENANCE.txt -> WARN
_what_makes_verify_FAIL.M6: no archive root found at all -> ERROR (this is the anti-silent-pass: an empty run is a failure, not a pass)
_what_makes_verify_FAIL.M7: a calibration_rounds.yaml round_binaries checksum claim does not resolve against the manifest -> ERROR

_example_archive._note: The SHAPE of one entry, for reading only. The placeholder SHA256 is deliberately NOT valid hex so it can never be mistaken for a real checksum or silently pass a hex check. --generate writes these fields; you write PROVENANCE.txt.
_example_archive.label: <ROUND>_<what_changed>_<short_commit>
_example_archive.sha256: <64-hex, computed by --generate from the binary on disk>
_example_archive.provenance_sha256: <the same value as read from the archive's PROVENANCE.txt; a MISMATCH is error M3>
_example_archive.change: one line on what the source change does; empty for an unmodified baseline build
